subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Bystander Effect
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Bystander Effect.

hook.text: Kitty Genovese was attacked while 38 neighbors allegedly watched. None called for help.

buildup.text: Darley and Latané found that the more people present, the less likely any individual is to intervene.

discovery.text: It's diffusion of responsibility: everyone assumes someone else will act. So nobody does.

twist.text: Alone with a victim, 85% help. In a group of five, only 31% do. The crowd doesn't help—it paralyzes.

climax.text: Knowing the effect helps. People trained about the bystander effect are significantly more likely to act.

punchline.text: In a crowd, nobody's job becomes everybody's excuse.
